description: Stratified inference rules. Stratum 0 = derived (deterministic function of observed values), 1 = inferred (value + checkable expected property, confidence >= thresholds.tau_inferred), 2 = extrapolated (philosophy-driven proposals, confidence capped by thresholds.extrapolation_cap, never an input to any rule). Within a stratum rules are monotone and applied in id order, so the fixpoint is unique. Conditions, value ops and predicates are closed sets implemented in code (include/loom/kb.h); rules only combine them.

expected_property.rationale: the current version is the highest version observed anywhere (git, snapshots or archives); it is never older than the newest git version
confirm_if: a later source names the same version as current
refute_if: an observed version higher than $value exists for the same lineage

expected_property.rationale: merged if a merged_into/evolved_into fact exists (merged_into = target); abandoned if an explicit abandon cue or no activity for thresholds.abandoned_after_days before corpus end without code; paused if an explicit pause cue or inactivity for thresholds.paused_after_days; active otherwise
confirm_if: an explicit status statement by the owner
refute_if: activity after the date the status was derived from

expected_property.rationale: implemented = an implements fact to a declared symbol/path in some codebase; partial = code evidence covers part of the name or the code carries TODO/'nie działa' cues; superseded = target of an active supersedes fact (superseded_by = source); abandoned = on the abandoned side of a fork, or explicit abandon cue, or no mention for thresholds.abandoned_after_days and no code; planned = only future-tense cues
confirm_if: a declared symbol for the component appears in a later snapshot
refute_if: the component is mentioned as working after being marked abandoned

expected_property.rationale: a UI framework or toolchain implies the platforms it targets (Kivy -> desktop + Android; Kotlin/JNI -> Android); the value is the union of implied platforms
confirm_if: a targets_platform fact for any listed platform
refute_if: an explicit statement that the app does not run on a listed platform

expected_property.rationale: the core language is the dominant language (by code volume) of the core modules; it must have a toolchain for every observed platform and no active decision may name another core language
confirm_if: a written_in fact for the subject
refute_if: an active decision choosing a different core language (e.g. a migration to C++)

expected_property.rationale: local-first + graceful degradation (MEGA MASTER §12) on every listed platform implies an embedded, file-based, offline-capable store; an analogous project's observed store is preferred
confirm_if: a stores_in fact with an embedded store
refute_if: a stores_in fact with a server-only store and no local cache

expected_property.rationale: stages are ordered by next_stage facts (A -> B -> C, numbered lists); unordered stages keep first-mention order
confirm_if: a second source lists the stages in the same order
refute_if: a next_stage fact that creates a cycle

expected_property.rationale: the chosen option is the option named by the latest active decision on the topic; it must be one of the options and must not have been rejected later
confirm_if: later conversations build on the option
refute_if: a later rejected_option item naming it

expected_property.rationale: when one option was chosen and the others were never revisited, they are implicitly rejected (abandoned != unimportant: they stay visible)
confirm_if: an explicit rejection of the option

expected_property.rationale: interfaces of a specified subject are the declared abstract types whose names co-occur with the subject
confirm_if: the spec names the interface
refute_if: the symbol is removed from the codebase

expected_property.rationale: files named like entry points (main.py, main.cpp, MainActivity.kt, server main) are entry points
confirm_if: the file defines main / an App subclass

expected_property.rationale: a version observed in archives or snapshots but above every git version exists only in the archives (source = archive)
confirm_if: a snapshot or attachment declaring the version
refute_if: a git tag or commit subject with the version

expected_property.rationale: an undated version is dated by its first anchored mention; the date must lie between the neighbouring versions of the same lineage
confirm_if: a snapshot file date or commit date for the version
refute_if: a mention of the version as existing before the inferred date

expected_property.rationale: components introduced or discussed in the same conversation unit as an anchored version mention are its features
confirm_if: an introduced_in fact
refute_if: the component exists in an older version's snapshot

expected_property.rationale: the base of a version is (a) an explicit based_on/'na bazie' statement, (b) the version whose snapshot shares the most unchanged files, (c) the latest version mentioned earlier; a base is always lower
confirm_if: an explicit based_on statement
refute_if: the snapshot contains changes only present in a different line

expected_property.rationale: two or more versions with the same base form a fork in the version DAG (e.g. 0.8.x and 0.9.0 both based on 0.7.10)
confirm_if: an explicit statement that the lines diverged
refute_if: one line contains the other's changes

expected_property.rationale: roles such as junior_dev/senior_dev/researcher are policy bundles defined as data, never classes (MEGA MASTER §4.7, §11)
confirm_if: roles defined in a data file
refute_if: a role hard-coded as a class or enum

args: ISyncTransport adapters: local files, zero-knowledge server, Google Drive (MEGA MASTER §4.12)

expected_property.rationale: sync is a contract with swappable adapters; local-first means the app works without any of them
confirm_if: an owner decision on sync

args: every stage is a TaskEngine task with input/output hashes and a checkpoint; intermediate representations are content-addressed artifacts

expected_property.rationale: constitution G: everything significant is resumable and auditable
confirm_if: the pipeline is ported onto the TaskEngine

args: agent actions are Task/Action records with checkpoint/retry/rollback on the Loom TaskEngine; roles are data (MEGA MASTER §1.3, §4.7)

expected_property.rationale: the historical agent becomes Loom's execution layer, not a separate application
confirm_if: an agent task kind registered on the TaskEngine
